blocks.heading: Operational Research Questions
blocks.text: This route operationalizes the mechanism-replacement direction by asking whether an averaged null-convergence condition can be relaxed from pointwise assumptions while still forcing trapped-surface formation. The first question targets the precise mathematical form of the explicit averaged null-convergence condition (A5) and how it differs from standard AANEC (A2), since AANEC alone may not imply the integrated focusing required for a Penrose-type argument. The second question fixes the Misner-Sharp compactness parameter (D4) for the restricted metric class, because a model-dependent threshold cannot be evaluated without a symbol-domain convention. The third question asks how stability of non-black-hole remnants (A6) is formally defined so as to distinguish the target class from regular black hole models such as Hayward or Bardeen. These questions are not answered by observation; they delimit the proof obligations PO1–PO3 and the counterexample search.

blocks.heading: Planned Contributions and Their Distinct Roles
blocks.text:
| Contribution | Role in the argument | Decision if unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| C1: AANEC plus explicit averaged focusing as an independent geometric hypothesis | Fixes the scope of P1 and separates averaged energy positivity from Raychaudhuri-type convergence | If A5 collapses into A2, the relaxation claim loses force and the theorem must be restated as AANEC-only |
| C2: Compactness-threshold criterion for trapped-surface formation | Supplies the bridge from focusing (S1) to a trapped surface (S2) via D4 | If D4 is ill-defined for the metric class, no numerical or formal threshold can be proposed |
| C3: Stability predicate for non-black-hole remnants | Defines the domain of P2 and separates the target class from horizon-bearing regular black holes | If A6 is undefined, candidate witnesses CE1 and CE2 cannot be adjudicated as counterexamples |
| C4: Counterexample boundary for averaged-focusing evasion | States the failure condition under which the theorem must be restricted | If witnesses satisfy all A1–A6 and evade trapping, the proposal is rejected within the declared class |

blocks.heading: Averaged Null Energy Condition and the Missing A5
blocks.text: The displayed relation is the AANEC integral along a null geodesic γ with tangent k^a, and it is the baseline assumption A2. The planned contribution C1 is not this integral itself but the additional explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition A5, whose exact mathematical form is currently unresolved. A5 must be stated as a condition on the expansion scalar θ or on an integrated Ricci-focusing term that is independent of A2, otherwise the relaxation from pointwise NEC/SEC to averaged assumptions does not by itself yield the convergence needed for S1. Quantum fields systematically violate pointwise energy conditions, which motivates the averaged formulation, but the gap between AANEC and the required integrated focusing remains the central unresolved dependency.

blocks.heading: Scope and Transition to the Formal Argument
blocks.text: The contribution of this section is therefore a decision matrix, not a completed theorem. It separates the formal claim that averaged focusing plus compactness forces a trapped surface from the astrophysical consistency constraint that the observed 2–5 solar mass gap may instead be governed by explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, or binary evolution. The next stage must convert the unresolved items into a compactness criterion and a stability predicate; until then, candidate witnesses CE1 and CE2 remain unadjudicated, and no outcome branch can be triggered.

claim_provenance.statement: What is the exact mathematical form of the explicit averaged null-convergence condition (A5) that distinguishes it from standard AANEC (A2)?
What is the formal definition of the Misner-Sharp compactness parameter C for this specific metric class (D4)?
How is the stability of non-black-hole remnants (A6) formally defined so as to distinguish it from regular black hole models like Hayward/Bardeen?
AANEC plus an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition is proposed as an independent geometric hypothesis for spherical collapse.
A model-dependent Misner-Sharp compactness threshold is proposed as the bridge from averaged focusing to trapped-surface formation.
A stability predicate for non-black-hole remnants is proposed to define the domain of the exclusion conclusion and separate it from regular black hole models.
A counterexample boundary is proposed for witnesses that evade averaged focusing, delimiting when the theorem must be restricted.
